note: Hand-kept, not extracted. The document opens its address section with an outline of which block begins at which address, printed as a figure in the right-hand column of a two-column page. It is a different table from the parameter address map -- two columns rather than seven -- so it is held here rather than merged into it.
why_it_is_here: It was missed twice: once because the parser reads the parameter address map and this is not that table, and once because the audit that was meant to catch the miss looked at the first cell of each line, which on a two-column page is the other column entirely. Recorded now so that the document's own account of where its blocks begin can be held against the regions the archive measured.
not_yet_joined: Nothing on the site reads this yet. The document's blocks are broad areas and the archive's regions are what a sweep found; holding one against the other needs a comparison that has not been written, and writing one that merely looks right would be worse than saying so here.
read_as: The figure is printed under one port heading, and three of its seven rows carry a mark to the right of the block name. The `port` here is that heading; the `group` is the mark, recorded as printed. The two say different things and are kept apart for that reason, which is the same reading the SC-88Pro's figure is held under -- there the same block appears under both port headings with a different mark in each, which is what the marks are there to distinguish.
not_resolved: What the marks stand for this page does not say, and no other page of this document prints a legend for them. `#A` is recorded as `#A` rather than resolved into a claim about which parts a block is common to.
